  1. Disaggregated prefill

Disaggregated prefill

Prefill processes the prompt and is compute-bound. Decode generates tokens and is memory-bandwidth-bound. Splitting them lets each pool scale and be sized independently.

Use it for long prompts, retrieval-augmented generation, and workloads where prompt length varies widely.

Complete values file 

namespace: models

hfSecret:
  enabled: true
  managed: false
  name: hf-secret

llmDefaults:
  image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b-disagg
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
      name: llama-3.1-8b-instruct

    # Decode pool
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --served-model-name
      - llama-3.1-8b-instruct
      - --enforce-eager
    replicas: 2
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

    # Prefill pool. Unset fields fall back to the decode pool above.
    prefill:
      replicas: 2
      args:
        - --model
        - /mnt/models
        - --enable-chunked-prefill
        - --max-num-batched-tokens
        - "8192"
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "16"
          memory: 64Gi
          nvidia.com/gpu: "2"

HF_TOKEN is injected into the prefill containers automatically, exactly as it is for the decode pool.

Minimal form

When both pools share the same image and arguments, an empty prefill is enough:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b-disagg
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
    prefill: {}

Sizing the two pools

Phase Bound by Favors
Prefill Compute Fewer, larger GPUs; high batch token limits
Decode Memory bandwidth and capacity More replicas; large key-value cache

Starting points:

Traffic Prefill Decode
Long prompts, short answers Larger pool Smaller pool
Short prompts, long answers Smaller pool Larger pool
Retrieval-augmented generation 2 x 2 GPUs 2–4 x 1 GPU

Different hardware per pool

Put prefill on the faster accelerator:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b-disagg
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    nodeSelector:
      accelerator: nvidia-a100
    tolerations:
      - key: nvidia.com/gpu
        operator: Exists
        effect: NoSchedule
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
    prefill:
      replicas: 2
      nodeSelector:
        accelerator: nvidia-h100
      priorityClassName: prefill-priority
      args:
        - --model
        - /mnt/models
        - --enable-chunked-prefill
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu: "2"

The decode pool lands on A100 nodes and prefill on H100 nodes. The prefill pool inherits the toleration because it does not define one.

Combining with multi-node decode 

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-70b-disagg
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --tensor-parallel-size
      - "4"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "16"
        memory: 128Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "4"
    parallelism:
      tensor: 4
      data: 8
      dataLocal: 4
    worker: {}
    prefill:
      replicas: 1
      args:
        - --model
        - /mnt/models
        - --tensor-parallel-size
        - "4"
        - --enable-chunked-prefill

The prefill pool inherits the image, resources, and placement from the decode pool, so only the differing arguments are listed.

Multi-node prefill

Spread the prefill pool across nodes with prefill.worker, mirroring the decode pool:

    prefill:
      parallelism:
        tensor: 4
        data: 8
        dataLocal: 4
      worker: {}

Give prefill workers their own placement when needed:

    prefill:
      worker:
        nodeSelector:
          accelerator: nvidia-a100
        priorityClassName: prefill-worker

Useful arguments

Argument Pool Purpose
--enable-chunked-prefill Prefill Splits long prompts into chunks
--max-num-batched-tokens Prefill Token budget per batch
--enforce-eager Decode Lower memory, no CUDA graphs
--max-num-seqs Decode Concurrent sequence cap

Is it worth it?

Disaggregation adds moving parts and total GPU cost. Start with the simpler layout in vLLM on GPU and adopt this only when measurements justify it:

  • Time-to-first-token is dominated by long prompts.
  • Prefill and decode utilization are clearly unbalanced.
  • You have enough GPUs for two separate pools.

Verify 

kubectl get llminferenceservice llama-8b-disagg -n models
kubectl get pods -n models -o wide
kubectl logs -n models -l app.kubernetes.io/name=llama-8b-disagg --tail=100

Measure time-to-first-token with a long prompt:

kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-8b-disagg 8080:80

time curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-3.1-8b-instruct",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the following: ..."}],
    "max_tokens": 64
  }' > /dev/null
